description: Build a rate limiter with sliding window and token bucket algorithms
prompt: Write a Python module with: (1) class `SlidingWindowRateLimiter` with __init__(self, max_requests: int, window_seconds: float), allow(self, client_id: str) -> bool, and get_stats(self, client_id: str) -> dict. (2) class `TokenBucketRateLimiter` with __init__(self, capacity: int, refill_rate: float), allow(self, client_id: str, tokens: int = 1) -> bool, get_stats(self, client_id: str) -> dict. Both must be thread-safe. Use time.monotonic() for timing. Include test_sliding_window() and test_token_bucket() testing: under-limit allows, over-limit blocks, window expiry re-allows, multi-client isolation. Use time.sleep() sparingly (<=0.1s) in tests.
expected_behavior: Both rate limiters correctly enforce limits, handle window expiry, and isolate clients

validation_criteria.l4: All test functions pass including timing-based tests
validation_criteria.l5: Thread-safe implementation, correct sliding window vs token bucket semantics, proper stats
